metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to all AI-assisted code, PR descriptions, and PR/issue comments; no numeric or volume threshold stated
domains.accountability_wording: it remains your responsibility to read through the whole thing and make sure that it makes sense to you and represents your ideas concisely

evidence.quote: Do not submit an AI-generated PR you haven't personally understood and tested, as this wastes maintainers' time.
it remains your responsibility to read through the whole thing and make sure that it makes sense to you and represents your ideas concisely
You can use any tools that help you understand the Zulip codebase and write good code, including AI tools.

domains.reasoning: The policy directly names AI use in coding and PR/comment communication, requires the contributor to understand, test, and take responsibility for AI-assisted output (human_in_the_loop), and explicitly states this is the contributor's own responsibility, satisfying both supervision level and accountability holder.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots; no supervision or accountability stated
domains.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md never discusses recording, transcription, or notetaker bots in meetings or discussions.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use for docs/blogs/design assets; no supervision or holder named
domains.reasoning: The guide's AI provisions cover code and PR/issue/community-chat communication, but never mention documentation, blog posts, or design assets specifically.

domains.rationale_only_mention: Maintainer time and attention is very limited, so it's important that changes you ask us to review represent your best work.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI in moderation actions; no supervision or holder named
domains.reasoning: Concern about consuming limited maintainer time/attention is used as a rationale for the code-contribution AI rules, but the policy never sets a rule about AI use in moderation actions themselves (e.g., issue triage, bans, content removal).

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on AI-assisted review by maintainers/reviewers
domains.reasoning: The document describes a human review process for PRs in detail but never addresses whether reviewers/maintainers may use AI tools to review contributions.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on autonomous/agentic AI acting on the repo
domains.reasoning: There is no mention of AI agents operating independently on issues, PRs, or the repository (Zulipbot is a rule-based workflow bot, not discussed as AI).

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy/water/carbon impact of AI use
domains.reasoning: The policy's concerns are about contributor understanding and maintainer time, not environmental cost of AI tools; no environmental language appears anywhere in the file.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware cost from AI use
domains.reasoning: No text in the file discusses server load, hosting costs, or hardware financing related to AI tools.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on project data/content being used to train models
domains.reasoning: The file never addresses whether Zulip's own issues, code, discussions, or user data may be used to train AI models; its AI discussion is about contributors using external AI tools, not the project's data being consumed for training.

unscoped_statements.quote: Do not post AI-generated messages in the Zulip development community -- we want to read your own genuine expression of your thoughts.
Successful contributors put in the reasoning and writing effort required to communicate clearly and succinctly, and don't waste the community's time with AI slop.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Zulip's CONTRIBUTING.md gives a detailed, human-in-the-loop policy specifically for AI-assisted coding and PR/issue/chat communication (contributor bears responsibility, must understand and test AI output, no AI-only PR descriptions or chat messages), but is entirely silent on notetaker bots, documentation/content, moderation actions, AI-assisted review, autonomous agents, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and use of the project's own data for training.

validation_problems: unscoped: quote not found in CONTRIBUTING.md
unscoped: quote not found in CONTRIBUTING.md

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
